analysis.title: Accelevation Holdings (ACCV): Takeaways from our investor lunch
key_insights: GS hosted an investor lunch in Boston with ACCV's CFO Ken Krause and Head of IR Larry De Maria. GS came away with more confidence in the longer-term growth algorithm and the datacenter infrastructure opportunity.

Management says the backlog is unaffected by recent volatility and fears because permitting and power are already secured for the late-stage pipeline. The pipeline is a multiple of the current backlog and shows no post-election slowdown.
ACCV now works with all five major hyperscalers, up from 2-3 at the IPO. Its share of wallet with them remains low. No single customer is more than 20% of revenue or the book.

ACCV sells a small but critical last-mile piece of datacenter buildouts where customers pay for speed to compute. Management says this supports pricing power. VRT is named as the primary competitor in white space, while others focus on stick builds.

Management targets about 30% incremental margins over time. Roll-off of legacy loss contracts, tied to a terminated construction partnership, created a 350bps year-to-date margin headwind. With these contracts 80-90% closed out, baseline margins would already be in the mid-20s.

SkyBridge modular platform gross margins are creeping over 30%, with a target of mid-30s at scale. Legacy stick-built projects are about 80-90% complete after $23mn of charges this year. The backlog includes contracts at high-30s to low-40s gross margins.

Power products are expected to reach 30-40% of the portfolio over time. Switchgear introductions are expected in the coming quarter. ACCV can attach power products (whips, PDUs, RPPs) because it is the basis of design in white space.

The backlog is $1.7bn, secured by firm commitments, LOIs or deposits. Management says it has never had a cancellation, because customers do not cancel near completion and contracts ensure payment even if delivery is delayed.

Estimates put leverage below 1.0x next year. Management plans disciplined M&A focused on technology additions (e.g. sidecars) and white space service capabilities. It wants to start buybacks once sponsor Olympus Partners, which holds about 86% of shares, begins to sell down.
The CEO spends about two-thirds of his time in factories and one-third with customers. 2027 priorities are scaling while keeping culture, factory-floor KPIs and better estimating processes.
GS expects a strong 4Q and constructive commentary on the full-year guide at that time. It rates ACCV Buy with a $20 12-month price target (11.0x Q5-Q8 EBITDA), 80.3% upside from $11.09.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after the investor lunch on its backlog, hyperscaler wallet share, pricing power and margin expansion. The target is based on 11.0x Q5-Q8 EBITDA.
Named by ACCV management as its primary competitor in white space. Covered by GS analyst Mark Delaney.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees an opportunity in mission-critical datacenter infrastructure, with a backlog that management says is unaffected by recent volatility.

earnings_insights: GS expects a strong 4Q for ACCV and constructive commentary on the full-year guide at that time.
GS estimates: EPS $0.29 for 12/25, $0.46 for 12/26E, $1.11 for 12/27E, $1.70 for 12/28E. Quarterly EPS estimates: $0.09 for 9/26, $0.14 for 12/26E, $0.20 for 3/27E, $0.24 for 6/27E.
GS estimates: revenue $911.0mn for 12/26E and $1,740.3mn for 12/27E, up from $447.8mn in 12/25. EBITDA is $160.3mn for 12/26E and $350.3mn for 12/27E, up from $90.9mn in 12/25.
The legacy loss contracts created a 350bps year-to-date margin headwind. $23mn of charges were taken this year on legacy stick-built projects.
risk_factors: Slowdown in data center capex spending.
Execution and project risk from rapid scaling.
Increased competition from large well-established companies.
Exposure to raw material price volatility and supply chain disruptions.
vol_and_positioning: Olympus Partners controls about 86% of ACCV shares. Management wants to start buybacks when the sponsor begins to sell down.
